name: Purchase and sale agreement
what: The signed contract to buy the property: price, deposits, deadlines, conditions, representations and remedies.

fields.label: Effective date
fields.definition: The date every contract period runs from, as the contract defines it, such as the last signature or the escrow agent's receipt of the signed contract.

fields.label: Buyer
fields.definition: The buying entity, and whether and to whom it may assign the contract, with any notice the assignment needs.

fields.label: Seller
fields.definition: The selling entity; compare it with the owner of record on the title commitment.

fields.label: Property
fields.definition: What is sold: the land by legal description or exhibit, the improvements, personal property, leases, service contracts and intangibles.

fields.label: Purchase price
fields.definition: The price, and any part of it paid other than in cash at closing.

fields.label: Earnest money
fields.definition: Each deposit: amount, the escrow agent holding it, the date it is due, the date it becomes non-refundable, and the events that return it.

fields.label: Feasibility period
fields.definition: Days the buyer has to investigate and terminate, with how the period ends and how notice of termination must be given.

fields.label: Title and survey periods
fields.definition: When the commitment and survey are due, the buyer's objection period, the seller's cure period, and what happens if the seller does not cure.

fields.label: Financing condition
fields.definition: Whether closing depends on the buyer getting a loan, the deadline, and how the buyer exercises it; none if the contract has no such condition.

fields.label: Closing date
fields.definition: The scheduled closing date, or the formula that sets it, and each extension right with its cost and notice deadline.

fields.label: Seller deliverables
fields.definition: What the seller must deliver during diligence and at closing, such as leases, operating statements, service contracts, estoppels, SNDAs, the deed, assignments and certificates, each with its due date.

fields.label: Seller representations
fields.definition: Each seller representation, how long it survives closing, and any cap or minimum on a claim for its breach.

fields.label: Closing conditions
fields.definition: Conditions to each side's duty to close, such as estoppels, issuance of the title policy and representations still being true.

fields.label: Default remedies
fields.definition: What each side can do if the other defaults: keep or recover the deposit, seek specific performance or damages, and any cap on recovery.

fields.label: Casualty and condemnation
fields.definition: What happens if the property is damaged or taken before closing: the size thresholds, termination rights, and who gets insurance proceeds or the award.

fields.label: Seller's non-foreign certification
fields.definition: Whether the contract requires the seller to deliver at closing a signed certification that it is not a foreign person, or provides for withholding instead.
